messages.author: e8e2387233c35cd4
messages.subject: Two-step task - ts_par6 - model regressors
parts:
Dear all,
thanks for the fantastic tool box. We are currently analysing imaging data of the two step task (Daw, 2011) and would like to include model regressors.

Model regressors are available for other models like the go-nogo task. 

We tried the following, but model regressors don't seem to be available yet:
output <- ts_par6(
+     data = dataALL, niter = 4000, nwarmup = 1000, nchain = 4, ncore = 4, modelRegressor = TRUE)

Is there a way around this? Or would this option only be included in an updated version of the code?

Thank you,
Franziska

messages.author: 47d1400f432367d7
messages.subject: Re: Two-step task - ts_par6 - model regressors
parts:
Hi Franziska,

Apologies for the late reply (assuming this is following up on a previous post re this question). I will include what I just sent to the previous post here for completeness: 

"
Currently, that model does not have model regressors available. Unfortunately, this means that the only way to do it would be to modify the raw stan code to get what you need. 

I am not sure when model regressors will generally be available across models—Young may be better suited to answer that than I am at the moment!
"

That said, if you would like to modify the Stan code, you can follow the example in the go/no-go models. e.g., lines 133-137 here show the basic idea: https://github.com/CCS-Lab/hBayesDM/blob/develop/commons/stan_files/gng_m1.stan, where you define variables that will store the values you are interested in. Then, you would need to include a list in the "regressors" argument of the function call (i.e. ts_par6(..., regressors = list(...))) that gives the names and dimensions of the variables of interests (corresponding gng example is here: https://github.com/CCS-Lab/hBayesDM/blob/develop/R/R/gng_m1.R). Additionally, you would need to specify the path to your modified stan model code using the "stanmodel_arg" argument when calling the function (i.e. ts_par6(..., stanmodel_arg = "path_to_stancode.stan")). 

This should allow you to extract information of interest—let me know if this is clear!

Best,
Nate

parts:
Dear Nathaniel/All,

Thank you so much for your suggestions.

We followed the steps that you mentioned to add regressors and tried running the model but it generates a few errors.

We are using the ts_par6 model as mentioned above. So we created a stan file with the same code as in file ts_par6.stan' and edited it to add our model regressors (using the code for the go/no-go models as an example as suggested).

Steps followed:

Changes based on the code in this link: https://github.com/CCS-Lab/hBayesDM/blob/develop/commons/stan_files/ts_par6.stan

1. Line no. 124 we added:
real reg_level1[N, T];

2. Line no. 185 we added:
reg_level1[i, t]   = v_mf[level1_choice[i, t]];  

(We would still need your help with the equations for the model regressors that we are interested in and this is just a dummy equation that we were trying to implement to see if the regressors are generated.)

3. After this, we saved this .stan file as 'ts_par6_reg.stan' into the folder 'stan_files' in the 'hBayesDM' folder.

4. We then called the function ts_par6 as below (using the code for the go/no-go models as an example as suggested, link: https://github.com/CCSLab/hBayesDM/blob/develop/R/R/gng_m1.R):

Code:
outputALL_in_6 <- ts_par6(
+     data = dataALL_in_corr, niter = 4000, nwarmup = 1000, nchain = 4, ncore = 4, regressors = list("reg_level1" = 2), stan_model(file = "/Users/prithasen/Summer_Project_TUM/Data/packrat/lib/x86_64-apple-darwin17.0/4.1.1/hBayesDM/stan_files/ts_par6_reg.stan"))

Error message:
Error in preprocess_func(raw_data, general_info, ...) :
  unused argument (regressors = list(2))

Alternatively, we also tried to add '==' instead of '=' while mentioning the regressor argument as below:

Code:
outputALL_in_6 <- ts_par6(
+     data = dataALL_in_corr, niter = 4000, nwarmup = 1000, nchain = 4, ncore = 4, regressors == list("reg_level1" = 2), stan_model(file = "/Users/prithasen/Summer_Project_TUM/Data/packrat/lib/x86_64-apple-darwin17.0/4.1.1/hBayesDM/stan_files/ts_par6_reg.stan"))

Error message:
Error in inits[1] : object of type 'S4' is not subsettable

Could you please help us with where we might be going wrong?

We would need the Model-free and Model-based Reward Prediction Errors as our regressors (parametric modulators) for the imaging analysis which is why we think we would need 'beta1', 'beta2' and 'w' from the model. We would be very grateful if you could please also help us with the equations that we would need for these conditions.

Many thanks in advance!

Hoping to hear from you soon!

Kind regards,
Pritha
